column3: Would you click one button to see if you are hurting someone?
In this experiment, a lot of people would not.
Students split money with a stranger. Option A: six dollars for you, one for them. Option B: five each.
When it was that clear, seventy four percent picked the fair one.
Then researchers hid one thing: what option A gave the stranger. Finding out took one free click.
And fair outcomes dropped by about half.
Researchers call it moral wiggle room. If you never look, you never have to feel unfair.
So, what are you not clicking on?
